item.title: China’s Economy Expanded 4.5% in Third Quarter, Powered by Exports
item.description: Economic growth accelerated, though consumer confidence and property market woes persist.

item.title: Saudi Arabia’s Military Limitations Are Being Exposed by Houthi Attacks
item.description: The kingdom has advanced weaponry, but the Yemeni militant group has proved to be a resilient foe.

item.title: Trump’s Overtures to Putin Put Republican Candidates in Hot Seat
item.description: GOP politicians in a number of tight races are breaking with Trump on Russia policy ahead of midterms.

item.title: Some Wall Street Leaders Are Weighing Bailing on ‘Davos in the Desert’ After Attacks on Riyadh
item.description: Recent attacks by Houthi rebels are making U.S. executives nervous to travel to the Future Investment Initiative conference in Saudi Arabia next week.

item.title: Putin Floats a Summit With Trump and Xi to Discuss Ukraine Deal
item.description: Ukraine’s Zelensky would not be included in the proposed talks, as Russia’s leader seeks to negotiate an end to the conflict that favors Moscow.

item.title: French Leaders Trade Blame After Rioting Sweeps the Nation
item.description: Police struggled to contain groups that attacked everything from city halls to luxury boutiques.

item.title: Trump Endorses Israel’s Netanyahu for Re-Election
item.description: The embattled Israeli leader had long sought Trump’s backing in tight elections scheduled for this month.

item.title: Ukrainian Drone Strike Hits Putin’s Hometown, Striking Oil Terminal
item.description: The fresh attack on Russian oil facilities came after President Trump’s efforts to enforce a fragile energy ceasefire collapsed.

item.title: Zelensky Takes a Risk by Publicly Confronting Trump Over Russia
item.description: Plus, masked Israeli settlers attack a group of European diplomats, and a playboy inherits the world’s most notorious mercenary force.

item.title: Alberta’s Secession Vote Opens Up a Bitter Divide in Canada
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney is trying to rally the oil-rich province to stick with the country at a time when national unity is needed.

item.title: How Zelensky Decided to Take the Risk and Publicly Confront Trump
item.description: The Ukrainian leader is calling out the White House for relaxing pressure on Russia, drawing more ire.

item.title: The Playboy Who Inherited the World’s Most Notorious Mercenary Force
item.description: The son of Wagner Group’s late founder hangs on to an African stronghold, making a fortune from guns, drugs and gold.

item.title: Violent Protests Rip Through Cities Across France
item.description: Mayhem broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in Paris, Marseille and elsewhere as resentment rises over affordability and budget cuts.

item.description: A pattern of escalating violence in the occupied territory is straining Israel’s relations with the West.

item.description: Nationalist parties have come to see President Trump as a liability and distanced themselves from him as they have been rising in the polls.

item.description: Tehran’s support is helping the Yemeni group mount its most potent attacks yet on the kingdom.

item.description: The company is digging in on its plans to lay off as many as 500 workers at its Stelco operations as the government weighs legal options to protect workers.

item.description: Kyiv lacks an answer, for now, to Moscow’s mass-produced new weapons.

item.title: Brazen Russian Attacks Are Testing NATO
item.description: The alliance is facing a dilemma over how to respond without escalating or looking weak.
